observation.visible_scene: A daytime waterfront cityscape viewed from the water, consistent with Istanbul's Golden Horn: a low bridge with two towers spans the left side, a long dark pier/bridge structure runs across the middle distance, and a dense hillside skyline with a prominent conical-roofed tower (Galata Tower) fills the right. The upper half is blue sky scattered with white cumulus clouds; the lower half is dark greenish-blue, choppy open water with patches of white foam (a wake) in the immediate foreground. Several light-colored boats sit moored along the right-hand quay.
visible_changes: The foreground water surface continuously churns: wave crests and troughs shift, and the white foam/wake patches at the bottom change shape, position, and intensity from frame to frame (e.g., foam near bottom-center early becomes more dispersed toward the lower edges later), indicating relative motion between the viewpoint and the water.
The distant bridge, pier, and skyline remain essentially locked in the same frame positions throughout the excerpt, with only negligible apparent shift, so no large camera pan or zoom is evident.
The cloud arrangement stays largely fixed against the sky across the segment; any drift is too subtle to confirm as real cloud motion versus camera parallax.
The moored boats on the right show no discernible movement relative to the quay.
No editing cut is visible; the sequence reads as one continuous shot.
outside_clip_unknowns: The actual speed, heading, and acceleration of the boat carrying the camera, and whether the wake pattern is from this vessel or another.
What lies beyond the right and left frame edges and behind the camera.
Whether the faint apparent background shift is boat translation, rocking, or a slow pan.
Any later change in scene or viewpoint after the crop ends.
uncertain_details: Whether the tiny apparent lateral/vertical jitter of the skyline is camera rocking on waves or a slow translational drift of the boat.
Whether the cloud field is genuinely moving or appears static only because the camera does not track it.
Exact identity of the small white shapes under/near the bridge (boats vs. reflections) given their low resolution.
static_intervals: The overall composition (sky, bridge, skyline) is effectively static; the only clearly ongoing physical process is the motion of the foreground water and wake.

Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.

Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
